# Summary of Conservative Party Manifesto 2024

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, saving an average worker approximately £1,350 annually. Self-employed individuals would see their main rate of National Insurance abolished entirely by Parliament's end. The party pledges not to raise income tax, VAT, or corporation tax rates.

For pensioners, a "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure the State Pension rises annually by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, while also increasing the tax-free allowance for pensioners to prevent the State Pension from being taxed.

## Public Services

The NHS would receive funding increases above inflation each year, with targets of recruiting 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Plans include expanding Pharmacy First services, building 250 GP surgeries, and establishing 50 Community Diagnostic Centres.

Education commitments include protecting per-pupil school funding in real terms, creating 60,000 additional school places for children with special educational needs, and introducing the "Advanced British Standard" for 16-19 education.

## Immigration

The manifesto proposes introducing a legally binding cap on migration, set annually by Parliament, with numbers falling each year. The plan includes continuing deportation flights to Rwanda and processing all asylum claims within six months.

## Housing

A target of 1.6 million homes in England is set for the next Parliament. Stamp Duty would be permanently abolished for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000, and a new Help to Buy scheme would be launched.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030. An additional 8,000 police officers would be recruited for neighbourhood policing.

## Energy and Environment

The party commits to net zero by 2050 while pledging annual oil and gas licensing rounds in the North Sea. Plans include tripling offshore wind capacity and building new nuclear plants, including Small Modular Reactors.
